title: Hawaiian Maui and the Fishing Hook
subtitle: A chant of Kualii describes land drawn from the sea

chant.work: Legends of Ma-Ui, a Demi God of Polynesia and of his Mother Hina
chant.author: W. D. Westervelt
chant.locator: Chapter II · MAUI THE FISHERMAN; Chapter II · MAUI THE FISHERMAN, normalized characters 24-536
chant.excerpt: Oh the great fish hook of Maui! Manai-i-ka-lani 'Made fast to the heavens'--its name; An earth-twisted cord ties the hook. Engulfed from the lofty Kauiki. Its bait the red billed Alae, The bird made sacred to Hina. It sinks far down to Hawaii, Struggling and painfully dying. Caught is the land under the water, Floated up, up to the surface, But Hina hid a wing of the bird And broke the land under the water. Below, was the bait snatched away And eaten at once by the fishes, The Ulua of the deep muddy places.
chant.note: Verbatim prose from Westervelt's early twentieth-century English compilation. Retain the named island/version; this is not a direct transcription of one oral performance.

narrativeBlocks.title: A hook with a name
narrativeBlocks.body: Westervelt prints a chant attributed to Kualii, about 1700, in which Maui's hook is named Manai-i-ka-lani, 'Made fast to the heavens.'

narrativeBlocks.title: The land rises
narrativeBlocks.body: Quotation from Westervelt's English compilation (whitespace normalized): “Oh the great fish hook of Maui! Manai-i-ka-lani 'Made fast to the heavens'--its name; An earth-twisted cord ties the hook. Engulfed from the lofty Kauiki. Its bait the red billed Alae, The bird made sacred to Hina. It sinks far down to Hawaii, Struggling and painfully dying. Caught is the land under the water, Floated up, up to the surface, But Hina hid a wing of the bird And broke the land under the water. Below, was the bait snatched away And eaten at once by the fishes, The Ulua of the deep muddy places.”

narrativeBlocks.title: A Hawaiian setting
narrativeBlocks.body: The chant names Kauiki, Hawaii, and Hina. Westervelt's surrounding account locates one version near Kauiki in the Hawaiian Islands.

narrativeBlocks.title: Attribute the chant as printed
narrativeBlocks.body: The quotation is Westervelt's English presentation of a chant he attributes to Kualii. Its date and wording are transmitted through his compilation and should not be treated as an independently verified original.

narrativeBlocks.title: A named island version
narrativeBlocks.body: The episode gives one Hawaiian account of Maui fishing up land; other islands preserve related but not identical Maui stories.
